summary.intent: Fix a layout bug where column headers in the bin interface of the web UI were stacking vertically instead of displaying in a single horizontal row, then deploy the fix via a PR.
summary.outcome: Identified and fixed a CSS specificity conflict by removing the redundant `file-list-header` class from the bin header element. The dev server was spun up against staging, the fix was verified, a branch was created, and the change was committed. PR creation was in progress at session end.

repo: The web app uses Vite, and CSS load order affects cascade resolution — globally-imported styles (via App.css) can override component-local styles when specificity is equal.

BinBrowser uses dual CSS classes on its header (`file-list-header bin-list-header`) while BinListItem correctly uses only its own class (`bin-list-item`), indicating an inconsistency in how the bin components were originally authored.
The staging API is at https://api-staging.cipherbox.cc and can be targeted by setting VITE_API_URL when starting the dev server.
Project is a monorepo under apps/web for the web UI frontend.

code.finding: The bin list header element had both `file-list-header` and `bin-list-header` classes. The base class defines a 3-column grid (1fr 120px 180px) while bin-list-header defines the correct 5-column grid (1fr 180px 100px 80px 90px). Removing `file-list-header` fixes the conflict.
bin-list-header is a self-contained class with all necessary styles (display, padding, font, border, grid-template-columns) — it does not need to inherit from file-list-header.
file-list-header defines a 3-column grid layout intended for the standard file browser, not the bin view which needs 5 columns.

workflow: CSS specificity bugs involving duplicate class names can be diagnosed by checking import order and cascade — when two single-class selectors define the same property, load order determines which wins.
Vite dev server can be pointed at a staging API via environment variable override at startup without modifying committed config files.

friction: Needed multiple rounds of file reads and grep searches to trace the CSS import chain and confirm the cascade conflict before identifying the root cause.
